name: Zombie-cell clearing implant
subtitle: an implant that sweeps out worn-out cells

effects.effect: clearing out worn-out 'zombie' cells makes old mice healthier
immune cells given a designed receptor hunt down a chosen target

effect: clearing out worn-out 'zombie' cells makes old mice healthier
how: As we age, cells that have stopped dividing but refuse to die pile up and leak the chemical signals that drive arthritis, stiff arteries and frailty; clearing them makes old mice visibly younger. A matchbox under the skin holds immune cells given a designed receptor that recognises a marker on worn-out cells, behind a membrane that lets the cells out only when a doctor opens a valve. One pulse a year, then the cells are designed to die off, so the hunt stops before it does harm.
obstacle: Worn-out cells share their markers with healthy ones that heal wounds and keep the liver running, so the hunt could cost more than it clears.
why: Turns a one-off mouse experiment into a controllable, repeatable yearly sweep in people.
real: Anti-uPAR senolytic CAR T cells improved metabolic health and exercise capacity in aged mice from a single dose (Nature Aging), but there is no human trial and nothing resembling an encapsulated implant with a valve for repeat dosing.
